Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address City Council on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other
matter within its jurisdiction subject to the rules of decorum described in Section 2.08.020 of the Norwalk Municipal Code.
If you wish to address City Council, please complete the card that is provided at the rear entrance to Council Chambers
and hand the card to the Sergeant at Arms. City Council will hear public comment on items listed on the agenda during
discussion of the matter and prior to a vote. City Council will hear public comment on matters not listed on the agenda
during the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the City Council:
   Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
   Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk’s department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted
listening devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda
and documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it has been
posted will also be made available for public inspection.

Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk’s Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard during
regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday – Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday; telephone (562)
929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e-mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  CLOSED SESSION MEETING

 Mayor Rios called the meeting to order at 5:01 p.m. in the Council Chambers, Norwalk
 City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard, Norwalk, California. Responding to roll call were
 Councilmembers Perez, Ramirez, and Valencia, and Mayor Rios. Vice Mayor Ayala
 arrived after roll call. Also present were Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager; Arnold M.
 Alvarez-Glasman, City Attorney; Gloria V. Ramirez, Deputy City Attorney; and Theresa
 Devoy, City Clerk.

 ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

 There were no persons wishing to address City Council on the matters to be discussed
 in closed session.

 City Council immediately convened to closed session for discussion on the following
 matters:

I.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – EXISTING LITIGATION PURSUANT TO
  GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 54956.9(d)(1) FCG Consultants, Inc. vs. City of
  Norwalk; Los Angeles Superior Court Case No. 241NWCV00016.

II.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – TORT LIABILITY CLAIMS PURUSANT
  TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54954.9(d): Claimants: AFNI (Maricela Cortez), Erika
  Barrero, Julianna Canchola, Julio Gutierrez, Sal Medina, Fernando Mendoza, Linda
  Porter, Ammeriah Quintero, Teresa Scott, and Jose Luis Vieryra.

 RECESS

 City Council recessed at 6:08 p.m. pending the commencement of the regular meeting.

  REGULAR MEETING

 Mayor Rios called the meeting to order at 6:18 p.m. in the Council Chambers, Norwalk
 City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard, Norwalk, California. Responding to roll call were
 Councilmembers Perez, Ramirez, and Valencia, Vice Mayor Ayala, and Mayor Rios. Also
 present were Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager; Arnold M. Alvarez, City Attorney; Gloria V.
 Ramirez, Deputy City Attorney; and Theresa Devoy, City Clerk.

March 19, 2024

The invocation was delivered by Danny Casas, Remnant Church; followed by the flag
salute, led by Private Jimenez, LCpl Kenneth L. Worley Young Marines.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

The City Attorney indicated that a briefing was provided and City Council direction was
given for Item No. I. He reported that City Council received a briefing for Item No. II and
unanimously voted to reject all claims and directed staff to bring a resolution to City
Council to consider delegating denial responsibility to California Joint Powers Insurance
Authority.

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

City Council reported on their attendance at the various baseball and softball league
opening day ceremonies. Councilmember Perez reported on her attendance at the
Norwalk Education Alliance mock interviews, and thanked those that volunteered and
participated; thanked the Public Safety staff and the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s
Department for their continued dedication to keep the City safe. Councilmember Valencia
reported on her attendance at the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department City Council
Academy; announced that the John Glenn High School Marching Band was invited to
participate in the 2025 Rose Parade; commented on her attendance at Artastic, thanking
the Parks and Recreation Department for its success; and shared that she attended the
Kiwanis 605 Dinner and Show Fundraiser. Councilmember Ramirez recognized the
Parks and Recreation Department for the continued success of all City events;
commented on the Veteran Villas and Park Improvement projects; announced the
upcoming Home Beautification Contest; requested staff consider establishing a Veterans
Commission; encouraged all to attend the Egg-Stravagant Egg Hunt on March 30; and
shared that Norwalk High School is hosting a Prom Outlet to assist teenagers who plan
to attend prom. Vice Mayor Ayala commended the Public Safety and Los Angeles
County Sheriff’s Departments for their continued efforts to keep the community safe and
thanked Ozzie Ramos, Director of Public Safety, and Lieutenant Garcia, Los Angeles
County Sheriff’s Department, for their successful collaborative efforts. Mayor Rios
reported on her attendance at Read Across America, the New River Park Playground
Ribbon-Cutting ceremony, CivicWell Policymakers Conference, Los Alisos Middle School
Career Day, and Norwalk High School’s Top Out event; commented on her
granddaughter’s participation on Norwalk’s soccer team and thanked all the Parks and
Recreation coaches who coach exceedingly well, and encouraged residents to register
for the 5K run occurring June 2.

SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION NO. 24-17 – BUDGET AMEDMENT - GRANT FUNDING FROM
  THE CALIFORNIA DEPARTMENT OF HOUSING AND COMMUNITY
  DEVELOPMENT’S CALHOME PROGRAM

Background:

On February 7, 2023, City Council approved the submission of an application to the California
State Department of Housing and Community Development for funding under the Calhome
Program (Program). The Program provides loans and grants to local public entities and
nonprofits for homeownership development projects, technical assistance for self-help housing
projects, first-time homebuyer mortgage assistance, owner-occupied rehabilitation assistance,
technical assistance for shared housing programs, and accessory dwelling unit/junior accessory
dwelling unit programs.

In November 2023, the City received a conditional grant award in the amount of $3,000,000 to
provide First Time Homebuyer Mortgage Assistance ($2,400,000) and Owner-Occupied
Rehabilitation Program ($600,000). Staff submitted the required documents to meet the
conditions of award acceptance. Staff will work with Global Urban Strategies, Inc. to administer
the Program. Global Urban Strategies, Inc. will be compensated directly from the administration
fees allocated by the Program funds.

Fiscal Impact:

A Fiscal Year 2023/24 budget amendment is required to reflect an appropriation of grant funds
for eligible project expenditures in an amount not to exceed $3,000,000. There are no local
match requirements. There is no impact to the General Fund.

SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION NO. 24-18 - CONSIDERATION OF DELEGATION OF CLAIM
  DENIALS TO THE CITY'S INSURANCE AUTHORITY

Background:

The City is a member of the California Joint Powers Insurance Authority (CJPIA), and pools its
self-insured liability claims and losses with other CJPIA members under a Memorandum of
Coverage. As part of the Joint Powers Agreement that created the CJPIA, the CJPIA provides
tort Liability Claims administration through an independent contractor on behalf of its members
defending and indemnifying members from liability claims under the Memorandum of Coverage.

In the current process, claims are filed with the Office of the City Clerk which are sent to the
Claims Administrator, the Claims Administrator thoroughly reviews and investigates the claims
and makes a determination whether the City is or is not at fault. If it is determined that the City
is not at fault, direction is provided to the City Clerk to place the claims on the agenda for City
Council to authorize the denial of the claims pursuant to the Government Code.

Interest has been expressed to delegate the responsibility of claim denial to the CJPIA, as they
do for some of their other members. California Government Code 935.4 provides for delegation
of the authority to act on claims to a designee other than the government board by way of a
resolution adopted by the City Council. Therefore, Resolution No. 24-18 has been prepared for
consideration and if it is adopted this evening, the denial process would immediately be
delegated to CJPIA. City Council would no longer receive agenda reports to deny the claims. All
denial, insufficiency, and late notifications would be sent by the Claims Administrator to the
claimants or their representatives rather than by the City.
